correctness.rationale: The degree-d homogeneous component excludes two distinct nonzero linear coefficients when m>1: the surviving coefficient of x_i^(d-p^s)x_j^(p^s) is nonzero since binom(d,p^s)=m mod p. An invertible cotangent action is sufficient by surjectivity on the maximal-ideal filtration, then finite dimensionality. For f with leading term a x_j, raising to p^s projects to the box of exponents <m, with injective Frobenius on individual coefficients even over an imperfect field. Writing that projection as b+y_j u in B[y_j]/(y_j^m), the coefficient of y_j^(m-1) in its m-th power is b(m u_0^(m-1)+bC); u_0 is a unit by its nonzero residue, b is nilpotent, so the second factor is a unit. This proves necessity and sufficiency of the nonlinear support rule, not only of the leading action. For m=1 all positive-degree monomials die under the d-th power. The remaining parameters yield the two counts and dimensions; over an algebraic closure the reduced locus is identified by its points using the Nullstellensatz on the determinant open set. The permutation charts are open and closed with irreducible torus-affine factors.
residual_risks: The bounded replay does not exhaust the full d=6 automorphism space. The geometric result is about the reduced parameter variety, not a group-scheme smoothness assertion.

originality.rationale: The strongest checked matches cover the pure-power branch, the leading monomial action, exponent two and the adjacent exponent p^e+1. Credit those cases and the classical ingredients. The supported distinction is the exact unrestricted set of ungraded coefficients and resulting census for general d=mp^s, especially m>1 and s>0, where divisibility in the smaller visible box is not divisibility in the original algebra. No inspected broader theorem implies that surviving distinction.
residual_risks: An older specialized modular classification could imply the mixed-exponent census. The inaccessible Deo–Maitra scan and bounded catalogue/literature checks do not establish priority.
